texts.preamble: The Member Secretary vs S.Ganavel on 23 March, 2023 Author: J.Nisha Banu Bench: J.Nisha Banu, S.Srimathy W.A. Before The Madurai Bench Of Madras High Court Reserved on : 24.04.2025 Pronounced on: 08.10.2025 Coram The Honourable Mrs. Justice J.Nisha Banu And The Honourable Mrs. Justice S.Srimathy Wa(Md). Nos.102, 103, 641, 642 of 2024, 890/2023, 1255 and 1256 of 2024 and CMP.(MD).Nos.15816/2023, 11654, 4649, 4650, 5412, 5804, 961//2024, 7083/2023, 959/2024 9702 and 9704 of 2024 --- The Member Secretary Medical Services Recruitment Board (Mrb) 7th Floor, Dms Building 359, Anna Salai Teynampet, Chennai-600 006 ...Appe vs. 1.S.Ganavel 2.S.Winston Churchill ...Respondents 1 in W.A.(Md).N 3.Archana ...Respondent No in W.A.103/20 3.The Secretary to Government Health and Family Welfare Department 1/35 The Member Secretary vs S.Ganavel on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16119482/ 1 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
texts.facts: The appellant/2nd respondent is directed to re-visit the selection process in favour of the respondent/petitioner in light of what has been held above. The revised selection list shall be published by the appellant/2nd respondent within the period of 4 weeks. The essential facts necessary for the disposal of the writ appeals are discussed hereunder:- 5.1. The appellants herein is the Medical Services Recruitment Board (MRB), Chennai who issued notification inviting applications from eligible candidates for direct recruitment to the post of Food Safety Officer on temporary basis in Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug Administration Department. The Commissioner, Tamil Nadu Food Safety and drug administration department, Chennai has sent proposals to fill up to fill up 131 posts as per Food Safety Subordinate Service rules and the same was approved by the Government in G.O.(D).No.975, Health and Family Welfare (M1) Department dated 27.08.2021 and thereafter notification dated 13.10.2021 came to be published by the Medical Services Recruitment Board (MRB). https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 09/12/2025 08:15:10 pm ) W.A.(MD).Nos.102, 103, 641, 642/2024 890/2023, 1255 & 1256/2024 5.2. The Respondents herein are the medical practitioners holding degrees in Siddha medicine and BDS(Bachelor of Dental Surgery).The applications submitted by the respondents were accepted and they were permitted to take a written examination on 20.10.2022. However, their names were omitted from the selection list published by the Board on the ground that degrees in Siddha Medicine and BDS does not fall within the definition of a degree in medicine. Aggrieved by such exclusion, the respondents filed writ petitions challenging the impugned selection list. 6. Out of the writ appeals under consideration, W.A(MD).No. 641 and 642 of 2024 relates specifically to the exclusion of candidates holding a Bachelor of Dental Surgery(BDS) degree, while the remaining appeals pertain to the exclusion of candidates possessing degrees in Siddha Medicine. 7. With respect to W.A(MD).Nos. 102, 103, 641, 642, 1256 of 2024 & 890 of 2023, the learned counsel appearing for the appellants submitted that as per the educational qualification prescribed in the notification dated https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 09/12/2025 08:15:10 pm ) W.A.(MD).Nos.102, 103, 641, 642/2024 890/2023, 1255 & 1256/2024 13.10.2021, among the The Member Secretary vs S.Ganavel on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16119482/ 9 other qualification mentioned, the "Degree in Medicine" has been notified as one of the prescribed qualification for the post of food safety officer. It is submitted by the learned counsel that as per Section 2(f) of the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956, the term "Medicine" means modern scientific medicine in all its branches and includes surgery and obstetrics, but does not include veterinary medicine and surgery, therefore, the said definition does not include other system of medicine such as Bachelor of Siddha in Medicine (BSMS)/M.D.(Siddha) and Bachelor of Dental Surgery(BDS). 7.1. In this regard, The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India have issued clarification in this regard on 12.10.2022. The said relevant portion is extracted hereunder:- "3. In this context, for the purpose of qualification of Food Safety Officer specified in Rule 2.1.3(1) of Food safety and Standards Rules, 2011, it may be clarified that:- i. The "degree" means the degrees as prescribed in Sub-section (3) of Section 22 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956 (3 of 1956). https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis For the "Degree in Medicine", Hon'ble High Court of Allahabad in the matter of WP No. 2754 of 2015 Dr. Amit Pandey and ORs. Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Ors observed that the degree in Medicine does not include any other system of medicine and it will not be proper to include or read any other degree awarded by councils under other acts in to degree of Medicine. Medicine is defined only under Indian Medical Council Act, 1956 and not in other enactments. iii. In respect of the "equivalent qualification", the Central Government has not notified any such equivalent qualification so far. Hence, the only qualifications specified for the Food Safety Officer in the above-mentioned rules are applicable for the post of Food Safety Officer." 8.
texts.arguments: It is also contended by the learned counsel for the appellants that the respondents qualifications viz., Bachelor of Siddha in Medicine (BSMS)/M.D. (Siddha), Bachelor of Dental Surgery(BDS) cannot be treated as other equivalent /recognised qualification, as they have not been notified as equivalent/recognised qualification by the Central Government. Since the respective respondents has not acquired the prescribed qualification for the post of Food Safety officer, they were not considered as eligible candidates under PSTM(Person studied in Tamil Medium) category. It is also pointed out that https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 09/12/2025 08:15:10 pm ) W.A.(MD).Nos.102, 103, 641, 642/2024 890/2023, 1255 & 1256/2024 Medical Services Recruitment Board (MRB) is recruiting agency and acts as per the rules provided by the intending authorities namely Head of the Department and the board does not have the power to include or exclude any qualification for the post decided by the employer. And therefore, the learned counsel for the appellant prayed to [LEAKAGE_MASK] the order passed by the learned Judge holding that the respondents were entitled to be considered for the post of Food Safety Officer" by quashing the selection list with the direction to issue a revised selection list by considering the respondents. The Member Secretary vs S.Ganavel on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16119482/ 10 9. Per Contra, the learned counsel for the Respondent submits that with respect to the issue of exclusion of a person holding Bachelor of Siddha Medicine and Surgery (BSMS) degree from a list of candidates for a Food Safety Officer position, the respondent made reference to an RTI response from the Ministry of AYUSH dated 05.08.2022 which states that Bachelors of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery (BAMS) and Bachelors of Homeopathic Medicine and Surgery (BHMS) are "equivalent to MBBS." The communication also clarified that these degrees are recognized medical qualifications under Section 2(h) and 35 of NCISM Act, 2020 and under section 2(f) and 35 of NCH https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 09/12/2025 08:15:10 pm ) W.A.(MD).Nos.102, 103, 641, 642/2024 890/2023, 1255 & 1256/2024 Act, 2020 respectively with a 5.5-year course duration, and they have postgraduate and PhD courses similar to MBBS and therefore it should be considered equivalent as well. 9.1. It is also further contented that the 'degree in medicine' from a recognised University as a qualification prescribed is to be read and understood including all forms of medicine particularly the medicinal courses governed under the provisions of Indian Medical Council Act, 1956 and National Commission for Indian system of Medicine Act, 2020. It is also stated that it cannot be denied for the reason that the course which the respondents underwent is neither scientific nor modern. It is to be noted that the duration of course, the prescribed training period, the subject taught and the syllabus covered are all scientific studies borne out of Research and absorbing modern techniques. 9.2. The learned counsel for the respondent relied on the similar recruitment notification which came to be issued by the Public service Commission of the State of Tripura, where the educational qualification for the post of Food Safety Officer was prescribed as follows:- https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 09/12/2025 08:15:10 pm ) W.A.(MD).Nos.102, 103, 641, 642/2024 890/2023, 1255 & 1256/2024 "Educational Qualification required for direct recruitment: A degree in Food Technology or Diary Technology or Bio Technology or Oil Technology or Agricultural Science or Veterinary Sciences or Bio-Chemistry or Microbiology Chemistry or Masters Degree in or BUMS/BSMS/MBBS/BAMS/BHMS/BDS for a recognized University." , which indicates that in the said notification, the term Bachelor Degree in Medicine has been elaborated and all the degrees granted in Medicine in the modern medicine are included. Therefore, the said Degree comes under the category "Medicine". 9.3. In support of the arguments placed, the respondent placed reliance on Judgment passed by the Maharashtra Administrative Tribunal, Mumbai Bench in Original Application Nos. 322, 360, 361 & 370 of 2023, wherein the government considered that Ayurveda is not Medicine and the degree in BAMS is not a degree in Medicine, but the tribunal interpreted the term "Medicine" and held that the said term must be understood with fullest meaning. Relying on this, the learned counsel for the Respondent prayed to dismiss the writ appeal and allow the respondents to be considered to the post of Food Safety Officer. With Respect to W.A(MD).Nos. 1255 of 2024 is concerned, the learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the respondent had prayed to https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis The expert's justification is that while PVC is a widely used plastic, it can be harmful to human health. Specifically, when melted, it releases a corrosive and toxic gas. For Question 62 (Batch-1): The correct answer is option 'A'-100 ppm. The expert clarifies that this is the correct answer based on the Prevention of Food Adulteration (PFA) Rules, 1955. They also noted that the rules from 1954 might have different sweetener limits, but the correct answer for this specific question is 100 ppm as per the 1955 rules. ? 10.1. The learned counsel for the appellant also submitted that a total of 120 candidates were provisionally selected for the post of Food Safety Officer, following a certificate verification process on 23rd and 24th March, 2023. The said list was published on 13.03.2023. The cut-off mark for the last candidate selected under the General Turn (GT) category was 77.76 and the cut-off mark for the last candidate selected under the Backward Class Muslim (BCM) https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis The respondent's score is 69.37 marks who belong to the Scheduled Caste (SC) category, whereas the last candidate selected under the SC category secured 70.12 marks. Since, the respondent's score is lower than the SC category cut-off mark, the respondent had not reached the selection zone and thereby prayed for setting aside the order passed by the learned single Judge directing to award marks for the same and consequently directing the appellants to re-visit the selection process in favour of the respondent. 10.2. Per contra, the learned counsel for the Respondent asserts that for Question No.16 Option (C) petroleum is the correct answer as petroleum is a raw material and therefore cannot be used for wrapping sweets. But the expert's provided answer, "Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC)" Option A, is incorrect because PVC can be used for wrapping sweets, as stated in the Food Safety and Standards Packaging Regulations 2018, specifically in Schedule-IV. For Question No. 62, it is asserted that this question is flawed because it asks for a single maximum limit for artificial sweeteners in carbonated water and soft drinks. However, according to the PFA Rules 1955, different artificial sweeteners have different maximum limits. For example, Saccharin Sodium's https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 09/12/2025 08:15:10 pm ) W.A.(MD).Nos.102, 103, 641, 642/2024 890/2023, 1255 & 1256/2024 limit is 100 ppm, Acesulfame Potassium's is 300 ppm, and Sucralose's is 300 ppm. Therefore, the question is wrong for not specifying which artificial sweetener it refers to and thereby the respondents are entitled to one mark for this. 10.3. The counsel for the respondent also contends that the reservation rules were not followed correctly in the provisional selection list as the published cut-off mark for the General Turn is 74.08, but the cut-off for the BCM General category is 74.97, which violates reservation policy. It was argued that the candidates from the BCM community who score higher than the General Turn cut-off should be included in the General Turn based on merit. Similarly, the respondent counsel The Member Secretary vs S.Ganavel on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16119482/ 12 claims that five candidates from the Scheduled Caste (SC) community who scored higher than the General Turn cut- off of 74.08 were "wrongly included" in the Scheduled Caste Turn instead of the General Turn. The petitioner notes that out of the 20 total posts for the Scheduled Caste Turn, only 17 candidates were provisionally selected, and therefore, three more SC candidates should be chosen. It is also stated that the SC Arunthathiyar Reservation was not followed correctly, as only two of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 09/12/2025 08:15:10 pm ) W.A.(MD).Nos.102, 103, 641, 642/2024 890/2023, 1255 & 1256/2024 four available posts were filled. They also argue that if suitable candidates from the Arunthathiyar community are not available, the remaining posts should be filled by other SC candidates, as per Section 27 of the Tamil Nadu Government Servants Conditions of Service Act, 2016. 10.4. To substantiate the case of the Respondent, the learned counsel for the Respondent cites the Supreme Court dictum of Anil Kumar Gupta vs. State of U.P., dated 28.07.1995 reported in 1998(5)SCC 173 which outlines the proper procedure for filling open competition and reservation quotas based on merit, as well as the Rajesh Kumar Daria vs Rajasthan Public Service Commissionreported in 2007 (8) SCC 785 which also supported this principle. 11. No. 2754 of 2015 [Dr. Amit Pandey & Ors. v. State of U.P.,] has categorically observed that the term 'Degree in Medicine' does not extend to or include any other system of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 09/12/2025 08:15:10 pm ) W.A.(MD).Nos.102, 103, 641, 642/2024 890/2023, 1255 & 1256/2024 medicine, and it would not be proper to construe or read into it degrees awarded by councils constituted under other enactments and that the expression 'Medicine' is defined only under the provisions of the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956, and not under any other statute. Qualification: Food Safety Officer shall be a whole time officer and shall, on the date on which he is so appointed possesses the following: (i) [a Bachelor's or Master's or Doctorate degree in Food Technology or Dairy Technology or Biotechnology or Oil Technology or Agricultural Science or Veterinary Sciences or Bio-Chemistry or Microbiology or Chemistry or medicine from a recognized University, or ] (ii) any other equivalent/recognized qualification [notified by the Food Authority with the prior approval of the Central Government], and (iii) has successfully completed training as specified by the Food Authority in a recognized institute or Institution approved for the purpose. Provided that no person who has any financial interest in the manufacture, import or sale of any article of food shall be appointed to be a Food Safety Officer under this rule" The rule indicates that for qualifying for the post of Food safety officer, one must hold the above said specifications, which includes "Degree in Medicine from a Recognised University".
